corrected_value.title: An Effort to Close Achievement Gaps at Scale through Self-Affirmation.

decisions.quote:
The current study was designed to replicate both the original self-affirmation study
(Cohen et al., 2006) and the previous successful independent replication (Borman et al., 2016).
decisions.reason: Neither prior_adjudication_path nor prior_state_path exists on disk (never adjudicated). Hanselman, Rozek, Grigg, & Borman (2017) explicitly state (e.g., lines 345-346, 355-359, 681-686, 868-928) that their study was designed to replicate both the original self-affirmation study by Cohen et al. (2006) (shipped row 301, 10.1126/science.1128317, coded at target_index 0) and the previous independent scale-up replication in the same school district by Borman, Grigg, & Hanselman (2016) ('An Effort to Close Achievement Gaps at Scale through Self-Affirmation', Educational Evaluation and Policy Analysis, 38(1), 21-42, 10.3102/0162373715581709; References lines 1076-1078). Using a new randomized trial in Cohort 2 (N = 1,269 seventh-grade students across all 11 district middle schools, including 449 Black and Hispanic students), the authors retest the district-wide self-affirmation GPA and achievement effects reported in Cohort 1 by Borman et al. (2016) and formally test for treatment-effect differences across the two cohorts (Table 2, Table 3, and Section 'Comparison to Previous Cohort', lines 868-928). Borman et al. (2016) is a distinct primary empirical paper from Cohen et al. (2006) and is absent from shipped_rows.
